Subject: MAP kickoff — deployment mode & region constraints

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As discussed, Acme Health needs a short mutual action plan that locks our deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and region constraints for our pilot and GA timelines. Our two primary asks:

- A clear decision cadence with acceptance criteria for each mode (we need to know what would qualify a Hosted PoC vs committing to Dedicated capacity or Private deployment).
- A firm timeline for procurement and go-live gates — target GA is Sept 15, 2027 but we need milestones for procurement signoff, SOC2 evidence review, and an operations handoff.

I've attached our initial MAP workbook (Acme_MAP_initial.xlsx) and included procurement on cc. We can be flexible with a hybrid approach, but compliance requires US-based processing for PHI-derived features and a documented fallback if Dedicated slots are delayed.

Can you propose a 6–8 week evaluation cadence and a minimal acceptance checklist we can share with our security and procurement teams? Also flag any artifacts you need from us (audit point-of-contact, expected TPS, inference SLA).

Samantha
CTO, Acme Health

Samantha — attaching our Redwood MAP template filled with a proposed cadence (MAP_Acme_20270408.xlsx). Key highlights below; the workbook has the detailed gates.

TL;DR recommendation: start with a Hosted PoC in US-East (non-PHI features) for 6 weeks, run acceptance traffic patterns (latency, 99th p50/p95), then decide by Gate 2 (week 6) whether to commit to Dedicated for peak traffic and a Private deploy (air-gapped or VPC-hosted) for PHI workloads.

Proposed gates and acceptance criteria (high level):
- Gate 0 (Week 0): Kickoff, onboarding, SOC2 artifact request (we need your SOC2 contact + expected audit window).
- Gate 1 (Week 2): PoC config verified (model variant, token budget, KV cache rules), throughput smoke test (baseline 10k daily requests simulated).
- Gate 2 (Week 6): Quality and latency SLOs met on Hosted PoC (p95 < 350ms, accuracy/regression threshold on evaluation set).
- Gate 3 (Week 10–12): If Gate 2 fails on cost/latency, commit to Dedicated capacity with pre-warm windows; Private deployments require security attestation and legal approval (procurement_trigger_date shown in workbook).

Risk notes:
- Private deployment adds ~6–8 weeks for on-prem packaging or VPC provisioning and KMS integration.
- Dedicated commitment provides predictable throughput but requires a monthly/annual capacity contract; we can design a burst policy to reduce upfront commit.

Next steps I propose: 1) Quick sync Mon Apr 12 to align acceptance SLOs with your security team; 2) Redwood provides SOC2 evidence index and initial SOW/DocuSign link for procurement to review.

Attachments: MAP_Acme_20270408.xlsx, SOC2_evidence_index.pdf

—Kim
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Kim / Laura — quick technical notes to add into Gate definitions (copying the MAP workbook):

- PoC (Hosted): We need a deterministic traffic replay for the first 7 days (sampled user messages + billing token projections). We'll set up continuous batching with prefix caching enabled for common prompts to reflect realistic latency/cost.
- Dedicated: request 4 x A100 equivalent reserved slots for expected peak if they commit to 100k tokens/day; capacity planning in workbook shows latency benefits with KV cache warmed.
- Private: list dependencies — KMS/HSM integration, VPC peering, and an on-prem installer for air-gapped customers (if they go private for PHI). Plan for a 6–8 week lead time after legal acceptance.

Fallback play: If Gate 2 fails only on cost, we can propose a temporary mixed routing policy — sensitive calls to Private (once provisioned) + user-facing low-sensitivity calls on Hosted with token limits. That allows GA cadence to remain while we finish Private.

I'll add a short ops checklist to the workbook for the infra handoff (runbook, playbooks for hotfix rollback).

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
